# Wire protocol reference

Clients (the desktop app, the Android app, the CLI, `infantry mcp serve`) talk to the daemon over one WebSocket,
`ws://<host>:<port>/ws`, authenticated with the daemon token. Every message is one JSON **envelope**:

```rust
pub struct Envelope {
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    #[ts(rename = "type")]
    pub r#type: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub data: String,
    /// Written out as `null` when absent.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub session_id: Option<String>,
    /// Per-session sequence (F2); written out as `null` when absent.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub sequence: Option<i64>,
    /// Contract 1.87.0 correlation id; omitted when null.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub request_id: Option<String>,
    /// Contract 1.125.0: who a `turn` frame came from; omitted when null.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub origin: Option<MessageOrigin>,
}
```

`type` is a frame name from the table below; `data` is the frame's payload, a JSON text. A request may carry a
`requestId` (contract 1.87.0); the answer to a correlated request (marked below) then comes back to that client only.

The full history of every frame and field, with the version that added it, is the wire contract text
`rust/crates/infantry-protocol/CONTRACT.md` in the repository. The protocol crate's test `contract_md_and_constants_agree` keeps it complete.
